sentence: The small intestine is the part of the digestive tract that runs from the pylorus of the stomach to the ileocaecal valve, where it meets the large intestine.
note: Runs from the gastric pylorus to the ileocecal valve; the valve separates the ileum from the large intestine (colon).

sentence: It has three regions, the duodenum, jejunum and ileum, and it is the site of most chemical digestion and almost all absorption.
note: Three regions proximal to distal: duodenum, jejunum, ileum; small intestine is the site of most chemical digestion and almost all absorption.

sentence: Enzymes from the pancreas and from the intestinal lining do most of the chemical digestion, and bile salts help to emulsify lipids in the duodenum.
note: Brush-border and pancreatic enzymes do the majority of chemical digestion (OpenStax); bile salts and pancreatic enzymes emulsify and break down lipids in the duodenum (StatPearls).

sentence: Duodenum, jejunum and ileum, in order from the stomach
note: Three regions listed proximal to distal.

sentence: From the pylorus of the stomach to the ileocaecal valve at the large intestine
note: Runs from the gastric pylorus to the ileocecal valve, which separates ileum from colon.

sentence: About three metres in a living person, roughly twice that in a cadaver
note: About 3.05 m (10 ft) in a living person; cadavers about twice as long because of lost muscle tone.

sentence: Mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria and serosa
note: Four layers from innermost to outermost: mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, serosa.

sentence: Circular folds, villi and microvilli (the brush border) greatly increase the surface area
note: Circular folds, villi and microvilli together raise absorptive surface area greatly; microvilli create the fuzzy brush border.

sentence: Coeliac trunk and superior mesenteric artery; veins drain to the portal vein
note: Arterial supply from celiac trunk and SMA; veins feed the superior mesenteric vein, which joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.

sentence: Gastroscopy with biopsy; blood tests and biopsy for coeliac disease
note: Gastroscopy checks food pipe, stomach and top of intestine, biopsy may be taken; coeliac diagnosis uses blood test and biopsy.

sentence: The three regions follow one another from the stomach, with no clear dividing line between the jejunum and the ileum.
note: Regions run proximal to distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum; no clear demarcation between jejunum and ileum.

sentence: The duodenum lies just below the stomach and curves around the head of the pancreas in a C shape.
note: Duodenum sits just below the stomach; pancreatic head lies within the C-curve of the duodenum (attribution within that response not explicit).

sentence: Its first part is intraperitoneal, whereas its second, third and fourth parts are retroperitoneal, lying behind the peritoneum.
note: First part intraperitoneal; parts two to four retroperitoneal; remainder lies behind the peritoneum.

sentence: The jejunum and ileum are also intraperitoneal, and the mesentery carries their blood vessels, nerves and lymphatics.
note: Jejunum and ileum are intraperitoneal organs; the mesentery carries the small intestine blood vessels, nerves and lymphatics.

sentence: The jejunum lies mainly in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen and the ileum mainly in the right lower quadrant.
note: Jejunum mainly left upper quadrant; ileum mainly right lower quadrant.

sentence: The ileum ends at the ileocaecal valve, which separates it from the large intestine.
note: Ileocecal valve separates the ileum from the large intestine (colon).

sentence: The duodenum is the shortest and widest part of the small intestine, and it has four parts: the bulb, the descending part, the horizontal part and the ascending part.
note: Duodenum shortest and widest (small intestine article); four parts: bulb, descending, horizontal, ascending (duodenum article).

sentence: Bile and pancreatic secretions enter the descending part through the ampulla of Vater, where the main pancreatic duct joins the bile duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla that opens into the duodenum.
note: Bile and pancreatic secretions enter via ampulla of Vater on the descending part; main pancreatic duct joins bile duct to form hepatopancreatic ampulla.

sentence: The ileum, the final region, is the longest part of the small intestine.
note: Ileum is the longest part of the small intestine; regions listed proximal to distal ending with ileum.

sentence: In life the whole small intestine is about three metres long, and in a cadaver it is about twice as long because muscle tone is lost.
note: About 3.05 m (10 ft) in a living person; cadavers about twice as long due to loss of muscle tone.

sentence: The regions also differ in what they absorb: the duodenum is the major site of iron absorption, while the terminal ileum absorbs vitamin B12, which needs intrinsic factor made in the stomach.
note: Duodenum is the major site of iron absorption; intrinsic factor, made in the stomach, is needed for B12 absorption in the terminal ileum.

sentence: The wall of the small intestine has four layers: the mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria and serosa.
note: Four layers innermost to outermost: mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, serosa.

sentence: Deep circular folds (plicae circulares), villi and microvilli together greatly increase the surface area available for absorption.
note: Circular folds, villi and microvilli together raise absorptive surface area greatly; plicae circulares defined as deep folds of mucosa and submucosa.

sentence: The microvilli give the mucosa a fuzzy appearance called the brush border, and the absorptive cells synthesise digestive enzymes and place them in the membranes of their microvilli.
note: Brush border is the fuzzy appearance created by microvilli; absorptive cells synthesize digestive enzymes and place them in microvillus membranes.

sentence: Cells that arise in the intestinal glands include absorptive cells, goblet cells, Paneth cells (which secrete lysozyme) and several types of enteroendocrine cell, and some of the hormone-secreting types occur only in the duodenum, or only in the duodenum and jejunum.
note: OpenStax table lists absorptive, goblet, Paneth, enteroendocrine cells; Paneth cells secrete lysozyme; glands are their source; some hormone types limited to duodenum or duodenum and jejunum.

sentence: Intestinal juice is a mixture of water and mucus.
note: Intestinal juice is a mixture of water and mucus.

sentence: The epithelial cells are renewed rapidly.
note: Epithelial cells renew quickly (a few days; figure not quoted).

sentence: The small intestine receives arterial blood from the coeliac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery.
note: Arterial supply comes from the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery.

sentence: In the duodenum, the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery supplies the upper part and the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery the lower part.
note: Superior duodenum fed by superior pancreaticoduodenal artery; inferior segment by inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

sentence: The jejunum and ileum are supplied by jejunal and ileal branches of the superior mesenteric artery, which run through the mesentery.
note: Jejunal and ileal branches of the SMA run through the mesentery.

sentence: Veins follow the arteries and drain into the superior mesenteric vein, which joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.
note: Small intestinal veins follow the arteries and feed the SMV, which joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.

sentence: Lymph begins in the mucosa and drains to nodes along the mesentery, the arterial arcades and the superior mesenteric artery, and from there to the coeliac nodes.
note: Lymph starts in the mucosa; drains to nodes along mesentery, arterial arcades, SMA; then celiac nodes.

sentence: Sympathetic fibres from the superior mesenteric ganglia reach the jejunum and ileum through the superior mesenteric plexus; they reduce secretion and motility and cause vasoconstriction.
note: Postsynaptic sympathetic fibres from superior mesenteric ganglia reach jejunum and ileum via superior mesenteric plexus; reduce secretion and motility, vasoconstriction.

sentence: In the duodenum, bile salts and pancreatic enzymes emulsify and break down lipids.
note: Bile salts and pancreatic enzymes emulsify and break down lipids in the duodenum.

sentence: Brush-border enzymes then complete the digestion of carbohydrates and proteins.
note: Brush border enzymes complete the digestion of carbohydrates and proteins.

sentence: Complex carbohydrates are first hydrolysed by salivary and pancreatic amylases, and only monosaccharides are absorbed by the lining cells, called enterocytes; proteins are reduced to small peptides and free amino acids.
note: Amylases hydrolyse complex carbohydrates, brush-border enzymes finish, only monosaccharides absorbed by enterocytes; proteins give small peptides and amino acids.

sentence: Blood capillaries in the villi take up carbohydrates and proteins, while the lacteals take up fats.
note: Blood capillaries in the villi take up carbohydrates and proteins, while lacteals take up fats (attributed to OpenStax Pharmacology page).

sentence: Enterocytes package fats into chylomicrons, which carry dietary fat and fat-soluble vitamins; these are too large for the basement membranes of blood capillaries, so they enter the larger pores of the lacteals.
note: Enterocytes package fats into chylomicrons carrying fat and fat-soluble vitamins; chylomicrons too large for capillary basement membranes so enter lacteals larger pores.

sentence: Water absorption follows osmotic gradients, helped by aquaporins in the intestinal membranes.
note: Water absorption thought to follow osmotic gradients, with aquaporins on intestinal membranes assisting.

sentence: Segmentation, in which rings of smooth muscle contract and relax, shoves chyme back and forth rather than moving it along the tract.
note: Rings of smooth muscle contracting and relaxing so chyme is shoved back and forth; does not move contents along the tract.

sentence: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition triggered by gluten that damages the lining of the small intestine: the finger-like villi flatten, so nutrients are absorbed less efficiently and deficiencies, iron among them, can follow.
note: Autoimmune condition triggered by gluten damages small intestine lining; villi flatten (villous atrophy); smaller absorptive surface gives deficiencies, iron an example (leaflets generally).

sentence: Crohn's disease is a long-term condition in which abnormal immune reactions cause inflammation in the digestive tract, most commonly in the small intestine and the beginning of the large intestine.
note: NIDDK: abnormal immune reactions cause inflammation in the digestive tract; most commonly affects small intestine and beginning of large intestine.

sentence: Ulcers can form in the duodenum as well as the stomach; the NHS names H. pylori infection and regular use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory painkillers as the main causes.
note: NHS page covers duodenal ulcers too; H. pylori infection and regular NSAID painkiller use are the main causes; H. pylori can cause duodenal ulcers.

sentence: Short bowel syndrome develops when the small intestine is shortened or damaged and cannot absorb enough nutrients, most often after surgery to remove part of it.
note: NIDDK: develops when small intestine is shortened or damaged and cannot absorb enough nutrients; most often caused by small bowel resection.

sentence: Small intestine cancers include adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, neuroendocrine tumours, gastrointestinal stromal tumours and lymphoma, and weight loss and abdominal pain can be signs, although other conditions can cause the same symptoms.
note: NCI patient PDQ lists adenocarcinoma, sarcoma, neuroendocrine tumours, GIST, lymphoma; unexplained weight loss and abdominal pain signs; other conditions cause same symptoms.

sentence: Persistent symptoms should be assessed by a clinician.
note: Generic caution, not a factual claim about anatomy.

where: section:How the small intestine is investigated
sentence: A gastroscopy checks inside the food pipe, the stomach and the top of the intestine using a thin tube with a camera, and a small sample of cells (a biopsy) may be collected.
note: NHS: test to check inside food pipe, stomach and top of intestine with thin camera tube; small sample of cells (biopsy) may be collected.

where: section:How the small intestine is investigated
sentence: The top of the intestine is the duodenum, the first region of the small intestine.
note: Gloss on NHS wording "top of your intestine"; returned text lists the duodenum as the proximal region, just below the stomach, but does not state the equivalence.

where: section:How the small intestine is investigated
sentence: The NHS says it can help find out what is causing digestive symptoms, and it can also be used for treatment, such as removing growths or stopping bleeding.
note: NHS: helps find cause of digestive symptoms; also used for treatment such as widening food pipe, removing growths or stopping bleeding.

where: section:How the small intestine is investigated
sentence: For coeliac disease, the NHS describes two main methods of diagnosis: a blood test that looks for antibodies and a biopsy that can help confirm the diagnosis.
note: NHS: two main methods are blood test for antibodies and biopsy to confirm; leaflets: blood tests for antibodies and small-bowel biopsy.
